key_insight: AutoEnergyDesign uses an LLM agent to optimize building energy systems, reaching a roughly €3.53 million net present cost with substantially fewer simulations than conventional optimizers.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce simulation effort when sizing integrated energy technologies, including photovoltaics, storage and heat pumps; it does not optimize solar cells themselves.
method: Propose constrained design changes using simulation history and procedural, semantic, episodic and reflective memory.
Evaluate eight energy technologies using year-long simulations and a 25-year net present cost objective.
Automatically keep or revert changes through git and record an auditable decision trace.
evidence_signal: In one measured-load building case study, LLM agents ran 10 trials of 50 simulations per model versus 10 seeds of 300 evaluations per baseline, achieving a best cost 1.20% below TPE and 0.23% below the evolution strategy.
watch_item: Results are limited to one building case study, and reliability varied by model: only Opus reached the best design in all ten runs.
paper_title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
